synopsis: Nested cross-validation is presented as the recognised method for removing optimistic bias caused by repeated machine-learning model and hyperparameter selection [f6993, f14330]. The glossary adds that it validates the choice of method inside the loop [f14330]. Chapter 9 identifies a three-way data split as the engineering analogue for addressing the same bias, and the glossary confirms that the booklet’s three-way tuning split is this equivalent [f6994, f14331]. These facts consistently describe the rationale, but provide no split proportions or measured bias reduction [f6993, f14330, f6994, f14331].

relations.note: Both identify nested cross-validation as removing optimistic bias from repeated model selection.
Both identify the three-way tuning split as the engineering equivalent of nested cross-validation.
Adds an engineering analogue for the bias-removal method.
Connects the glossary method to the booklet’s three-way tuning split.
